prompt: A teammate posts a MUST ACK addressed to you asking for example-URL exports before they write fix receipts. What do you do first?
chosen: Acknowledge as 'taken' immediately, then reply in-thread with one concrete plan line naming what you will pull and where the exports will land. The teammate needs to know the item is owned, not that it was seen.
rejected: Ack silently as 'noted' and start the pull without telling anyone; the teammate re-asks tomorrow because nothing in the thread says anyone owns it.

prompt: Why reply inside the owning issue thread instead of posting a feed update?
chosen: The teammate reads the thread for their item; a feed post gets missed between their own pulls. Thread replies keep the triage sequence together: ask, plan, receipts, fix receipts — one auditable line.
rejected: Post to the feed so everyone sees activity; threads are for files, the feed is for status. If the teammate misses it, that is their problem.

prompt: You dispatched the read-only browser pull for the example URLs. Is the work done?
chosen: No. Dispatch is not delivery. The exports land only when the payload is verified — counts match, URLs are verbatim, buckets are labelled per property — and then posted to #15. A task accepted and forgotten is the same as never sent.
rejected: Yes — the task was accepted by the browser, so the export is effectively on its way; reporting 'dispatched' closes the item until someone asks.

prompt: The teammate needs example URLs for GSC's flagged buckets. Why pull GSC's own example lists rather than crawling the sites yourself?
chosen: GSC's examples are the URLs Google actually flagged; a self-run crawl finds plausible URLs but not the flagged ones. Verify against the source of the finding, not a second opinion of your own.
rejected: Crawl the sites yourself — the lists are faster and probably the same URLs anyway; exactness of the source list is a detail.

prompt: How many example URLs per bucket do you bring back, and how do you report them?
chosen: A bounded sample (about 25 per bucket) plus the full count per bucket, grouped by site and bucket, verbatim URLs. The teammate needs the count for scope and samples for pattern-spotting; a raw dump of thousands is not an export, it is a liability.
rejected: Bring back every URL GSC lists, unsorted, in one giant block — completeness matters more than the teammate's ability to read it.

prompt: همکاری شما در روم درخواست کرده قبل از نوشتن رسیدهای فنی، نمونه ای از آدرس های مشکل دار دریافت کند. پاسخ مناسب شما چیست؟
chosen: پیام او را با حالت taken تایید می کنم و در همان ترد پاسخ می دهم که کدام نمونه ها را از کدام گزارش استخراج می کنم و نتیجه را در همان issue منتشر خواهم کرد. او باید بداند کار دست کی است نه اینکه فقط دیده شده است.
rejected: بدون پاسخ کاری را شروع می کنم؛ تایید و اطلاع رسانی هدر دادن وقت است و او فردا دوباره می پرسد چه کسی دارد این کار را انجام می دهد.
